title: Comm: The Gate Is in the Axon

scenes.tts: In comm mutants, Slit is still at the midline, and Robo is still made. Yet almost no axon crosses. Why?
scenes.visual: Title card: Comm, The Gate Is in the Axon. The comm ladder with almost no rungs; Slit at the midline; Robo on the axons.
scenes.narration: In comm mutants, Slit is still at the midline, and Robo is still made. Yet almost no axon crosses. Why?

scenes.tts: The rule offers one answer. The axon hears Slit too early. If so, Comm's job is to keep Robo down before crossing.
scenes.visual: Push meter on a precrossing commissural axon reads high. Label: too early?
scenes.narration: The rule offers one answer. The axon hears Slit too early. If so, Comm's job is to keep Robo down before crossing.

scenes.tts: How would you test that with genetics alone? In 1998, Tear, Goodman and colleagues did two experiments.
scenes.visual: Names and year on screen. Two experiment cards.
scenes.narration: How would you test that with genetics alone? In 1998, Tear, Goodman and colleagues did two experiments.

scenes.tts: First, make a fly lacking both robo and comm. Will it look like comm, like robo, or something new?
scenes.visual: Three tiles: robo ladder, comm ladder, and a blank tile for robo;comm with a question mark.
scenes.narration: First, make a fly lacking both robo and comm. Will it look like comm, like robo, or something new?

scenes.tts: It looks like robo. Follow it step by step.
scenes.visual: The blank tile fills with a robo-like ladder, thick rungs.
scenes.narration: It looks like robo. Follow it step by step.

scenes.tts: In a comm mutant, Robo is too high before crossing. Axons are repelled early and do not cross.
scenes.visual: Step 1 on screen: comm, Robo too high, no crossing.
scenes.narration: In a comm mutant, Robo is too high before crossing. Axons are repelled early and do not cross.

scenes.tts: In the double mutant there is no Robo one at all. So there is no Robo one to be too high.
scenes.caption: In the double mutant there is no Robo1 at all. So there is no Robo1 to be too high.
scenes.visual: Step 2: Robo1 crossed out entirely.
scenes.narration: In the double mutant there is no Robo1 at all. So there is no Robo1 to be too high.

scenes.tts: With Robo one gone, losing Comm changes nothing. The embryo shows only the robo phenotype.
scenes.caption: With Robo1 gone, losing Comm changes nothing. The embryo shows only the robo phenotype.
scenes.visual: Step 3: the Comm switch is shown disconnected; robo phenotype only.
scenes.narration: With Robo1 gone, losing Comm changes nothing. The embryo shows only the robo phenotype.

scenes.tts: This reasoning is called epistasis. When one gene only turns another down, the double looks like the gene turned down. That is the downstream gene.
scenes.visual: Label: epistasis. Arrow: Comm ⊣ Robo. The double mutant tile points to the Robo end; Robo highlighted as downstream.
scenes.narration: This reasoning is called epistasis. When one gene only turns another down, the double looks like the gene turned down. That is the downstream gene.

scenes.tts: Second experiment, the reverse. Make Comm in every neuron, at a modest level. What happens to the ladder?
scenes.visual: Every neuron in the cord lights up with Comm. Label: modest level. Blank ladder, question mark.
scenes.narration: Second experiment, the reverse. Make Comm in every neuron, at a modest level. What happens to the ladder?

scenes.tts: Robo protein falls, and the ladder looks like robo. Ipsilateral axons cross, and commissural axons recross.
scenes.visual: Robo stain fades everywhere; the ladder's rungs thicken.
scenes.narration: Robo protein falls, and the ladder looks like robo. Ipsilateral axons cross, and commissural axons recross.

scenes.tts: Extra Comm everywhere turns Slit hearing down everywhere. Much stronger Comm can give a more severe, slit-like collapse.
scenes.visual: Every growth cone's ears dimmed, not gone. Small inset: stronger Comm, slit-like ladder.
scenes.narration: Extra Comm everywhere turns Slit hearing down everywhere. Much stronger Comm can give a more severe, slit-like collapse.

scenes.tts: So Comm is not a second cue. It sets how much Robo the axon has, and when.
scenes.visual: On screen: Comm sets how much Robo, and when.
scenes.narration: So Comm is not a second cue. It sets how much Robo the axon has, and when.

scenes.tts: How does it do that? In 2002, Keleman, Dickson and colleagues proposed a sorting model.
scenes.visual: Cell animation begins: a commissural neuron with Golgi, endosomes and lysosomes. Label: sorting model, 2002. Names on screen: Keleman, Dickson.
scenes.narration: How does it do that? In 2002, Keleman, Dickson and colleagues proposed a sorting model.

scenes.tts: Comm is made in commissural neurons for a short time, before and during crossing.
scenes.visual: A timeline under the neuron: Comm on before and during crossing, off after.
scenes.narration: Comm is made in commissural neurons for a short time, before and during crossing.

scenes.tts: Inside the neuron, it meets newly made Robo. It diverts it away from the surface, into late endosomes and lysosomes.
scenes.visual: New Robo leaves the Golgi; Comm redirects it from the surface route into late endosomes and lysosomes.
scenes.narration: Inside the neuron, it meets newly made Robo. It diverts it away from the surface, into late endosomes and lysosomes.

scenes.tts: There, Robo is destroyed. The growth cone crosses carrying little Robo.
scenes.visual: Robo broken down in the lysosome; the growth cone crosses with few receptors.
scenes.narration: There, Robo is destroyed. The growth cone crosses carrying little Robo.

scenes.tts: Once the axon has crossed, the neuron stops making Comm. Robo reaches the growth cone.
scenes.visual: Comm fades; Robo flows to the growth cone surface.
scenes.narration: Once the axon has crossed, the neuron stops making Comm. Robo reaches the growth cone.

scenes.tts: Now the Slit it just crossed repels it.
scenes.visual: Slit binds the new Robo; the growth cone turns away from the midline.
scenes.narration: Now the Slit it just crossed repels it.

scenes.tts: Sorting is real. In living embryos, Comm stops a tagged Robo from reaching the axon tip.
scenes.visual: A fluorescently tagged Robo stays in the cell body and never reaches the tip when Comm is present.
scenes.narration: Sorting is real. In living embryos, Comm stops a tagged Robo from reaching the axon tip.

scenes.tts: But it is not the whole story. Flies whose Robo cannot be sorted develop normally.
scenes.visual: A Robo variant that Comm cannot divert; a normal ladder beside it.
scenes.narration: But it is not the whole story. Flies whose Robo cannot be sorted develop normally.

scenes.tts: Yet they still need Comm to cross. So Comm has at least one more way to hold Robo back.
scenes.visual: Remove Comm from those flies: the rungs vanish. A question-mark box labelled second Comm activity.
scenes.narration: Yet they still need Comm to cross. So Comm has at least one more way to hold Robo back.

scenes.tts: What that is remains debated.
scenes.visual: Label: still debated.
scenes.narration: What that is remains debated.

scenes.tts: For prediction, you need only the result. While Comm is present, Robo one stays low, and the axon hears Slit only weakly.
scenes.visual: Summary card: while Comm is present, Robo1 stays low and the axon hears Slit only weakly.
scenes.narration: For prediction, you need only the result. While Comm is present, Robo1 stays low, and the axon hears Slit only weakly.
scenes.caption: For prediction, you need only the result. While Comm is present, Robo1 stays low, and the axon hears Slit only weakly.
